chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Repeating the comedy as a little Buck and Bubbles, with mugging
summary: Their own tap numbers were separate from the borrowed jokes; kids repeating the pair's lines and facial mugging made the audience laugh.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you remember how the routines --
like how was the tap integrated into that? That was just comedy, but how was tap integrated into their act?
Well, I mean Bubbles tap danced in his act, but we couldn't -- we had our tap dances, was what Nat Nazarro saw us do, like "Sweet Sue" and "Broadway Melody" and "Bugle Call Rag", you see.
Well, was the comedy that you're talking about, was that comedy you would do, or was that comedy that Buck and Bubbles would do?

That was comedy that they would do, but we, by us being children like that, a little Buck and Bubbles, it was so funny if it was repeated, like if you heard a funny joke, and every time someone would repeat this joke, you would laugh, because it was just that funny, and they had a way of -- a delivery, a way of speaking, you see.
So you would repeat the jokes that they had already done.

Just some of them. Just some of them. Like run out -- we'd run through the -- like run out on the stage, like while they're out there, you know, and they would be looking, you know. Every time one of us would say something, you understand. It really was a comical idea.
Because Negros, at that time with the face, the eyes --

-- and all, you know. And he'd look -- when the other one would say something, he'd look over there, you know, and when the guy punched the line (Unintelligible) -- they'd jump back, you know, and the people would laugh.
